**CampusNotes: Open-Access Academic Portal and AI-Powered Study Assistant**

Prepared according to IEEE Std 830-1998 (Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications). Version 1.0.

# **1. Introduction**

## **1.1 Purpose**

This document is the Software Requirements Specification (SRS) of CampusNotes. It describes what the system shall do, the people who use it, and how well it shall perform. It is written for the project supervisor, the development team and the testers. All later design, coding and testing work shall be traceable to the requirements in this document.

## **1.2 Scope**

**Product name:** CampusNotes

**What the system will do**

- Show a searchable, filterable catalog of university courses to students without any login.
- Present the notes of each course as a structured set of modules in a reading view with sidebar navigation.
- Generate an AI summary and 4 key takeaways for the module that the student is reading.
- Provide a subject-isolated MCQ quiz with instant green/red feedback, explanations and a final score report.
- Track student reading progress and quiz performance.
- Let a system administrator manage courses, modules and MCQ banks.

**What the system will not do**

- Student registration, password reset or any mandatory login for student readers (by design).
- Conversion of user-uploaded PDF files (content is entered as text or Markdown).
- Payments, subscriptions or any other monetization.
- Native mobile applications (the product is a responsive web application).
- Live video streaming or real-time classroom hosting.

**Benefits:** one place for all course material, faster revision through AI summaries, and targeted self-assessment, with zero access friction.

## **1.3 Definitions, Acronyms and Abbreviations**

| Term               | Meaning                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| SRS                | Software Requirements Specification, the document that lists what the system must do                 |
| IEEE 830           | A standard that describes how to write an SRS                                                        |
| FR / NFR           | Functional Requirement (what the system does) / Non-Functional Requirement (how well it does it)     |
| Use case           | One goal that a user can achieve with the system                                                     |
| Actor              | A person or system that interacts with CampusNotes (Student, System Administrator)                   |
| Module             | One structured part of a course's notes. A course contains many modules (1:N).                       |
| MCQ                | Multiple-Choice Question. A quiz contains MCQs of one subject only.                                  |
| AI Note Summarizer | The feature that reads a module and returns a short summary and 4 key takeaways                      |
| FCP                | First Contentful Paint, the time until the first content appears on screen                           |
| TLS                | Transport Layer Security, the encryption used by HTTPS                                               |
| PII                | Personally Identifiable Information                                                                  |
| XSS                | Cross-Site Scripting, an attack that injects malicious script into a web page                        |
| WCAG               | Web Content Accessibility Guidelines                                                                 |
| Admin              | System Administrator                                                                                 |

# **2. Overall Description**

## **2.1 Product Perspective**

CampusNotes is a new, self-contained web application. It is built with Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS on the front end, Node.js server routes on the back end, and a relational database. It uses one external service, an AI summarization API, which the server calls with a key kept in the server environment. Students use a web browser on a desktop or mobile device; administrators use a protected admin area at `/admin`.

## **2.2 Product Functions**

- Browse, search and filter the course catalog.
- View course details and read module notes.
- Generate an AI summary and 4 key takeaways for a module.
- Take a subject-isolated quiz with real-time feedback and view the result.
- Track completed modules and the last visited module.
- Manage courses, modules and MCQ banks (administrator).

## **2.3 User Characteristics**

| User                 | Characteristics                                                                                          |
|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Student              | University student of computer science or engineering. Uses a phone or laptop. No training is needed. Does not log in. |
| System Administrator | Faculty or staff member who maintains course content. Basic computer skills. Logs in at `/admin` with protected credentials. |

## **2.4 General Constraints**

- The website shall be built with Next.js (App Router) and Tailwind CSS.
- The system shall not store personal information (PII) of students.
- Questions of different subjects shall never be mixed in one quiz.
- The AI summary shall consist of a short summary and exactly 4 key takeaways.
- Admin content shall be entered as plain text or Markdown, not as raw PDF files.

## **2.5 Assumptions and Dependencies**

- Users have a working internet connection and a modern web browser.
- The external AI summarization service is available. If it is not, the system degrades gracefully (see NFR-11).
- Course content and MCQ banks are prepared and loaded by the administrator before students use them.

# **3. Specific Requirements**

## **3.1 External Interface Requirements**

**User interfaces**

| Screen                                  | Description                                                                                  |
|-----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Home Page (`/`)                         | Course directory grid, search bar and category filter tabs                                   |
| Module Reader (`/notes/[courseId]`)     | Active module text, module index drawer and the AI Summarizer trigger                        |
| AI Summarizer Drawer                    | Side drawer showing the summary and key takeaways beside the reading text                    |
| Quiz Interface (`/quiz/[subjectId]`)    | MCQ page with real-time green/red feedback and collapsible explanations                      |
| Score Report                            | Score percentage, correct and incorrect counters and a retake button                         |
| Admin Panel (`/admin`)                  | Dashboard for managing courses, module text and MCQ banks                                    |

**Software interface: AI Note Summarizer API**

| Field          | Details                                                                                  |
|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Endpoint       | `/api/summarize` (POST)                                                                  |
| Input          | `{ "moduleId": "string", "content": "string" }`                                          |
| Output         | `{ "summary": "string", "keyTakeaways": ["point 1", "point 2", "point 3", "point 4"] }`  |
| Authentication | Internal server endpoint; the API key is held in the server environment                  |

**Communication interface:** all browser-server communication uses HTTPS (TLS 1.3).

**Hardware interface:** none. The product runs on standard user devices and a web server.

## **3.2 Functional Requirements**

| ID    | Functional Requirement                                                                                                             |
|-------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| FR-01 | The system shall display a responsive directory of all university courses on the homepage.                                         |
| FR-02 | The system shall allow users to search and filter courses by title, subject code or academic category.                             |
| FR-03 | The system shall display course details and provide access to a dynamic module reading view.                                       |
| FR-04 | The system shall grant instant reading access to study modules without registration or login.                                      |
| FR-05 | The system shall process active module text through an AI Summarizer to generate a summary and 4 key takeaways.                    |
| FR-06 | The system shall load subject-isolated MCQs per quiz session, mapped 1:1 with the selected subject.                                |
| FR-07 | The system shall validate MCQ choices instantly, highlighting options green (correct) or red (incorrect).                          |
| FR-08 | The system shall render a detailed answer explanation panel immediately after an MCQ option is selected.                           |
| FR-09 | The system shall calculate score metrics (total correct, percentage score) on quiz completion.                                     |
| FR-10 | The system shall track student progress, including completed modules and last visited module.                                      |
| FR-11 | The system shall allow administrators to manage courses, create unlimited dynamic modules per course (1:N) and maintain MCQ banks. |
| FR-12 | The system shall store users, courses, modules, summaries, progress records, quizzes and results in a database.                    |

### **3.3.3 Formal Use Case Specifications**

#### **UC-01: Browse Courses**

| Field          | Details                                                              |
|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Primary Actor  | Student                                                              |
| Description    | The student views the catalog of all available courses.              |
| Preconditions  | At least one course exists in the system.                            |
| Postconditions | The course cards are displayed with title, code and category.        |
| Related FR     | FR-01, FR-04                                                         |

**Main Flow**

1. The student opens the homepage.
2. The system loads the course directory.
3. The system displays the courses as a responsive grid of cards.

**Alternative Flow:** If no course exists, the system shows the message "No courses available yet."

**Exception Flow:** If the course data cannot be loaded, the system shows "Courses unavailable" and a "Reload" button.

#### **UC-02: Search Courses**

| Field          | Details                                                                      |
|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Primary Actor  | Student                                                                      |
| Description    | The student searches courses by title or subject code.                       |
| Preconditions  | The course directory is displayed.                                           |
| Postconditions | Only courses that match the search text are displayed.                       |
| Related FR     | FR-02                                                                        |

**Main Flow**

1. The student types a title or subject code (for example "CS-301") in the search bar.
2. The system matches the text against course titles and codes as the student types.
3. The system updates the displayed cards within 150 ms.

**Alternative Flow:** If the student clears the search bar, the system shows all courses again.

**Exception Flow:** If nothing matches, the system shows "No matching courses found."

#### **UC-03: Filter Courses**

| Field          | Details                                                                  |
|----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Primary Actor  | Student                                                                  |
| Description    | The student narrows the catalog by academic category.                    |
| Preconditions  | The course directory is displayed.                                       |
| Postconditions | Only courses of the selected category are displayed.                     |
| Related FR     | FR-02                                                                    |

**Main Flow**

1. The student selects a category tab (for example "Computer Science").
2. The system filters the course cards by that category.
3. The system updates the displayed cards within 150 ms.

**Alternative Flow:** If the student selects "All", the system removes the filter.

**Exception Flow:** If the category has no courses, the system shows "No courses in this category."

#### **UC-04: View Course Details**

| Field          | Details                                                                             |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Primary Actor  | Student                                                                             |
| Description    | The student opens a course to see its details and the list of its modules.          |
| Preconditions  | The course exists.                                                                  |
| Postconditions | The course details and the module index are displayed.                              |
| Related FR     | FR-03, FR-04                                                                        |

**Main Flow**

1. The student selects a course card.
2. The system loads the course metadata (code, title, university, category).
3. The system displays the module index of the course.

**Exception Flow:** If the course cannot be found, the system shows "Course not found" and a link to the homepage.

#### **UC-05: Read Module Notes**

| Field          | Details                                                                             |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Primary Actor  | Student                                                                             |
| Description    | The student reads the notes of one module in the reading view.                      |
| Preconditions  | The course has at least one module with content.                                    |
| Postconditions | The module text is displayed and the module is recorded as the last visited module. |
| Related FR     | FR-03, FR-04, FR-10                                                                 |

**Main Flow**

1. The student selects a module in the sidebar index.
2. The system loads the module content.
3. The system displays the content in the reading pane.
4. The system records the module as the last visited module.

**Alternative Flow:** The student switches to another module using the sidebar at any time.

**Exception Flow:** If the module content fails to load, the system shows "Module unavailable" and a "Reload" button.

#### **UC-06: Track Progress**

| Field          | Details                                                                         |
|----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Primary Actor  | Student                                                                         |
| Description    | The student views the number of completed modules and the last visited module.  |
| Preconditions  | The student has opened at least one module.                                     |
| Postconditions | The progress summary is displayed.                                              |
| Related FR     | FR-10                                                                           |

**Main Flow**

1. The student opens the progress view of a course.
2. The system reads the stored progress for the student.
3. The system displays the completed module count, the progress percentage and the last visited module.

**Alternative Flow:** The student selects the last visited module to continue reading from there.

**Exception Flow:** If no progress exists, the system shows "No progress yet. Start reading a module."

#### **UC-07: Use AI Note Summarizer**

| Field          | Details                                                                                 |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Primary Actor  | Student                                                                                 |
| Description    | The system generates a summary and 4 key takeaways from the module being read.          |
| Preconditions  | The student is viewing a module reading page (`/notes/[id]`).                           |
| Postconditions | The summary and 4 key takeaways are displayed beside the module text.                   |
| Related FR     | FR-05                                                                                   |

**Main Flow**

1. The student clicks "Generate AI Summary" in the sidebar drawer.
2. The system extracts the active content text of the module.
3. The system sends the text to the AI summarization backend.
4. The system formats the response as a markdown summary and 4 key takeaways.
5. The system displays the result in the sidebar drawer beside the module text.

**Alternative Flow:** The student closes the drawer to continue reading the raw module text.

**Exception Flow:** If the AI service does not respond within 2.5 seconds, the system shows "Summary unavailable. Please refer to module text." Reading and quizzes remain fully usable.

#### **UC-08: Take Quiz**

| Field          | Details                                                                                                 |
|----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Primary Actor  | Student                                                                                                 |
| Description    | The student takes a subject-isolated MCQ quiz and receives instant feedback on every answer.            |
| Preconditions  | The course and module exist and an MCQ bank for the subject is loaded.                                  |
| Postconditions | All answers are evaluated and the attempt is saved as a quiz result.                                    |
| Business Rule  | A quiz shall contain questions of the selected subject only (0% cross-subject questions).               |
| Related FR     | FR-06, FR-07, FR-08, FR-09                                                                              |

**Main Flow**

1. The student opens the subject page and clicks "Take Quiz".
2. The system loads the subject-isolated questions mapped to the Quiz ID.
3. The student reads a question and selects an option.
4. The system validates the choice instantly: a correct choice is highlighted green; an incorrect choice is highlighted red and the correct choice is also highlighted.
5. The system expands the explanation box with the explanation text.
6. The student repeats steps 3 to 5 until all questions are answered.
7. The system computes the score (Score = Correct / Total x 100) and saves the attempt.

**Alternative Flow:** If the student leaves midway, progress up to the current question is retained locally.

**Exception Flow:** If question data fails to load, the system shows "Quiz content unavailable" and offers a "Reload Quiz" button.

#### **UC-09: View Quiz Results**

| Field          | Details                                                                                          |
|----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Primary Actor  | Student                                                                                          |
| Description    | The student views the performance report of a completed quiz and may retake the quiz.            |
| Preconditions  | The student has answered all questions of a quiz (UC-08).                                        |
| Postconditions | The score report is displayed; a retake resets the quiz session.                                 |
| Related FR     | FR-09                                                                                            |

**Main Flow**

1. The system displays the score report after the last answer.
2. The report shows total attempts, correct count, incorrect count and percentage score.
3. The student reviews the report.

**Alternative Flow:** The student clicks "Retake Quiz"; the system resets the session and returns to the first question.

**Exception Flow:** If the result cannot be displayed, the system shows "Result unavailable" and a "Reload" button.

#### **UC-10: Manage Courses**

| Field          | Details                                                                   |
|----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Primary Actor  | System Administrator                                                      |
| Description    | The administrator adds, updates and removes courses in the master catalog.|
| Preconditions  | The administrator is logged in at `/admin`.                               |
| Postconditions | The course catalog reflects the change.                                   |
| Related FR     | FR-11, FR-12                                                              |

**Main Flow**

1. The administrator opens the course management page.
2. The administrator chooses Add, Edit or Delete.
3. The administrator enters or changes the course data (code, title, university, category).
4. The system validates and saves the change.
5. The system shows the updated course list.

**Alternative Flow:** The administrator cancels the action and no data is changed.

**Exception Flow:** If validation fails (for example a duplicate course code), the system shows an error message and does not save.

#### **UC-11: Manage Modules**

| Field          | Details                                                                       |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Primary Actor  | System Administrator                                                          |
| Description    | The administrator creates and edits the modules of a course (1:N).            |
| Preconditions  | The administrator is logged in and the course exists.                         |
| Postconditions | The module list of the course reflects the change.                            |
| Related FR     | FR-11, FR-12                                                                  |

**Main Flow**

1. The administrator selects a course and opens its module list.
2. The administrator adds a module or edits an existing one (title, order, text or Markdown content).
3. The system validates and saves the module.
4. The system shows the updated module list in order.

**Alternative Flow:** The administrator changes the order of modules.

**Exception Flow:** If the content is empty or invalid, the system shows an error message and does not save.

#### **UC-12: Manage MCQ Banks**

| Field          | Details                                                                           |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Primary Actor  | System Administrator                                                              |
| Description    | The administrator manages the MCQ question bank of each subject.                  |
| Preconditions  | The administrator is logged in and the subject exists.                            |
| Postconditions | The question bank of the subject reflects the change.                             |
| Business Rule  | Every MCQ belongs to exactly one subject.                                         |
| Related FR     | FR-06, FR-11, FR-12                                                               |

**Main Flow**

1. The administrator opens the MCQ bank of a subject.
2. The administrator adds or edits a question with its options, the correct option and the explanation.
3. The system validates the question (at least 2 options, exactly one correct option, explanation present).
4. The system saves the question to that subject only.

**Alternative Flow:** The administrator deletes a question; the system removes it from the bank.

**Exception Flow:** If validation fails, the system shows an error message and does not save.

## **3.4 Non-Functional Requirements (Quantified)**

Every requirement below has a measurable target and a way to verify it.

### **Performance (latency)**

| ID     | Requirement                              | Measurable Target                                                         | Verification                         |
|--------|------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| NFR-01 | Page load time                           | First Contentful Paint (FCP) of 1.2 seconds or less on a standard network | Lighthouse audit on the main pages   |
| NFR-02 | Interaction latency                      | Filtering, tab switching and quiz validation complete within 150 ms       | Browser performance profiler         |
| NFR-03 | AI summary latency                       | Summary and 4 takeaways rendered within 2.5 seconds of the click          | Timed test of `/api/summarize`       |
| NFR-04 | Concurrent usage                         | Supports 200 simultaneous students with all targets above still met       | Load test                            |

### **Security**

| ID     | Requirement                              | Measurable Target                                                                          | Verification                         |
|--------|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| NFR-05 | Transport encryption                     | 100% of traffic over HTTPS using TLS 1.3                                                   | SSL/TLS scan of the deployed site    |
| NFR-06 | Zero PII collection                      | 0 personal data fields (name, email, password) collected from student readers              | Database and form inspection         |
| NFR-07 | Input sanitization                       | 100% of dynamic parameters (for example `/notes/[id]`) sanitized; 0 XSS or injection findings | Security scan and manual test      |
| NFR-08 | Admin credential protection              | Admin passwords stored only as salted hashes; admin session expires after 30 minutes of inactivity | Code review and session test    |

### **Uptime and reliability**

| ID     | Requirement                              | Measurable Target                                                                          | Verification                         |
|--------|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| NFR-09 | System availability                      | 99.5% uptime or better during academic semesters (at most about 3.6 hours of downtime in a 30-day month) | Uptime monitoring report |
| NFR-10 | Data isolation in quizzes                | 0% cross-subject questions in any quiz session                                              | Automated test on all MCQ banks      |
| NFR-11 | Graceful degradation                     | If the AI service fails, reading and quizzes stay 100% operational and a fallback notice appears within 2.5 seconds | Fault-injection test |

### **Usability and compatibility**

| ID     | Requirement                              | Measurable Target                                                                          | Verification                         |
|--------|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| NFR-12 | Responsive layout                        | Layout works from 320 px (mobile) to 2560 px (4K desktop) without horizontal scrolling      | Browser device emulation             |
| NFR-13 | Accessibility                            | WCAG 2.1 Level AA with color contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1                              | Automated accessibility audit        |

## **6. Conclusion**

This SRS defines the requirements of CampusNotes, an open-access academic portal and AI-powered study assistant for PTUT students. It specifies 12 functional requirements, 12 formal use cases with a system use case diagram, and 13 quantified non-functional requirements covering latency, security, uptime and usability. Together with the traceability matrix, these requirements give the development team a clear and testable basis for design, implementation and testing. The 16-week work plan shows how the project moves from analysis and design to development, testing and deployment.
